claims.text: TOR-TILD’s standard EAM references inadequately represent the breadth of high-temperature liquid atomic configurations in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The proposed reference potential would supplement EAM with explicit many-body and angular-dependent interaction terms.
The proposed potential would be calibrated directly against high-temperature DFT liquid configurations.
A machine-learning-informed potential is a viable implementation for describing both solid and liquid states of a high-entropy material.
Explicit many-body and angular-dependent terms can capture the diversity of local structural environments found in ab initio alloy liquids.
The corrected potential will better capture the full spectrum of atomic arrangements in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Representing multi-atom interactions will reweight the energetic landscape so that it better reproduces the full ab initio liquid ensemble.
A better representation of the liquid ensemble will increase phase-space overlap between the reference potential and the ab initio target.
Increased reference–target phase-space overlap will reduce mismatch along the thermodynamic-integration path.
The proposed potential will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s standard EAM references.
The reduction in thermodynamic-integration path error could be approximately 50% or more.
The method is applicable to equiatomic or near-equiatomic metallic high-entropy alloys containing four to five or more elements, including Cantor-like alloys.
The proposed temperature range is approximately 0.9 Tm to Tm.
High-entropy-alloy liquids near melting exhibit considerable configurational diversity.
The enhanced potential is expected to work best when atomic-size differences and chemical complexity are moderate.
The potential’s effectiveness may diminish for systems with extreme atomic-size disparities or under far-from-equilibrium conditions.

The hypothesis is falsified if the corrected potential fails to produce a statistically significant 25–50% improvement in path-mismatch error and also fails to improve structural overlap metrics relative to the EAM control.
